confirmed.quote: Under the new test, an exhaustive census finds no nimber above star with at most six pawns on ordinary boards up to four files wide, but star two appears with seven
confirmed.problem: The headline holds only for the default race rule (count). The abstract names the e.p.-aware test but not the race rule, and the paper itself contradicts the unscoped sentence. With the e.p.-aware test and the opponent rule, six-pawn *2 positions exist, for example W a3 b3 c2 / B b5 b7 c6 on three files. Conversely, A and B (the seven-pawn *2) are not *2 under the opponent rule.
confirmed.evidence: I ran cylcgt: W a3 b3 c2 / B b5 b7 c6 is *2 at opponent/aware and opponent/textbook (and is not *2 under count or mover). realchess/certify/REPORT.md section 0 items 2-3 and RESULTS.md section 1 say the same: the 'no *k, k>=2' census result is the count rule, e.p.-aware test (atlas/flat8/compare_ep_aware.out). Inside the paper, 09_real.tex:45 and 08_star2.tex:58 say 'In non-default settings a few other census positions are *2', and Table 'Values of the Three *2 Positions' shows A and B as 'not *2' under the opponent rule. 01_intro.tex:43-44 scopes it correctly as 'default setting (count rule, e.p.-aware test)'.
confirmed.fix: Write 'Under the new test and the count rule, an exhaustive census finds ...' (or 'in the default setting'). Do the same for the sentence's second clause (seven pawns).

W a3 b3 c2 / B b5 b7 c6 on three files has six pawns and is *2 under the opponent rule (it is a long outcome-L game under count and mover). Position A, W a4 b3 d2 d3 / B a7 b7 c5, is *2 under count and a non-nimber under opponent. The evidence files agree: realchess/certify/REPORT.md section 1 gives candidate 2 as *2 under opponent, with e.p. on and both tests, and RESULTS.md section 1 limits "no *k, k>=2" to the count rule, e.p.-aware test. The abstract (00_abstract.tex lines 5-8) names the e.p.-aware test but never the race rule, so its census sentence is literally false for opponent/aware. 02_rules.tex line 104 makes "default" the standing convention, and 01_intro.tex lines 43-44, 08_star2.tex lines 5, 49, 64 and 109, and 14_conclusion.tex line 19 all scope the claim correctly. But the abstract never defines "default" and never mentions race rules, so a reader of the abstract alone cannot recover the scope. The auditor's one overstatement is "contradicts itself". confirmed.quote: $1/8$ and $\upsec\star$ \lab{C2}, and Tiny~1 \lab{C1}, occur in 10-man positions that can arise in a game.
confirmed.problem: 'Can arise in a game' is an unlabeled claim stronger than the repository evidence. For the 1/8 there is a hand-built pawn-capture history, and for up-second-star and Tiny 1 only a hand-checked pawn-move history. The evidence files say the up-second-star and Tiny 1 structures pass necessary legality conditions only. A retrograde check including all the pieces and the kings is listed as not done.
confirmed.evidence: RESULTS.md section 6: 'The other surviving positions pass necessary 8x8 legality conditions only.' atlas/flat8/REPORT.md lines 88, 172 and 183 (reachability 'beyond the necessary conditions checked' and 'Run a full retrograde reachability check of the candidate pawn structures with kings' are open items). atlas/flat8/rerun/REPORT.md C5: 'hand-built capture history' for the 1/8 mirror only. paper/ieee/REVIEW_LOG.md R10: the history was 'checked by hand'. The sentence is also repeated in 07_targets.tex:48-49 ('each a 10-man position with a legal pawn history').
confirmed.fix: Weaken to 'occur in 10-man positions whose pawn structures can arise by legal pawn moves and captures (hand-built histories; no full retrograde check with all pieces)', or label it as such.

verdict.reason:
Real, but low severity and confined to the intro sentence. The intro (01_intro.tex:41-42) says the 10-man positions "can arise in a game", with no label. That claim is about whole positions: all pieces, both kings, and the g4/g5 pawns. The evidence supports only pawn-level legality. RESULTS.md section 6 says "The other surviving positions pass necessary 8x8 legality conditions only". atlas/flat8/analyze.py, in the pawn_legality docstring, says "Sufficiency is not claimed (no full retrograde analysis)". atlas/flat8/rerun/REPORT.md says "necessary conditions only, plus a hand-built capture order for the 1/8 mirror", and a full retrograde proof game is still an open question. delegate/REVIEW.md T3 accepts the 1/8 mirror as reachable only "with a hand-built capture history". paper/ieee/REVIEW_LOG.md R10 says the up-second-star and Tiny 1 histories were "checked by hand".

Attempts to refute it:
- The histories are not wrong. I replayed all three by hand at pawn level, and each ends on the stated structure. The 1/8 history is c2xb3, a7-a5, b7xa6, c7xb6. The up-second-star and Tiny 1 history is c2xb3, b3-b4-b5-b6, a7-a6, then c7-c5 or c7-c6. Black's b7 and white's a2 and b2 never move, and the capture counts are plausible. No obstruction is visible, so the claim is probably true. It is unproven at the whole-position level, and nothing in the repository proves it.
- Two parts of the audit are inaccurate. The caption at 07_targets.tex:48-49 already says "a legal pawn history", which is correctly scoped, so it is not a repeat of the overclaim. The 07_targets.tex:66 and :82 sentences say "this pawn structure can arise" and "both pawn structures arise", and each gives the explicit moves. They are scoped to pawn structures, and a reader can check them. Only the intro wording overreaches. The audit's own suggested wording is also too heavy for the paper's plain voice.
verdict.better_fix: Make the intro match the caption's scope. In 01_intro.tex lines 41-42, replace "occur in 10-man positions that can arise in a game." with "occur in 10-man positions with a legal pawn history (Section~\ref{sec:targets})." Optionally, add one plain sentence at the end of the Up-Second Star and Tiny~1 subsection, after "(c7--c6 for Tiny~1).", in 07_targets.tex around line 82: "We checked these pawn histories by hand; we have not built a full game that also removes the other pieces." The same sentence would cover the 1/8 history at line 66. Leave the Fig. caption and the section title as they are. Do not add a new label, because this is a hand check and not a P/C1/C2 result.

confirmed.quote: otherwise by one fixed game $t$ with $-2\BIG\le t\le 2\BIG$; the choice of $t$ is the \emph{draw treatment}

The oracle the evidence actually computes treats the classes separately, so Theorem 18(c) (draws count as wins for black, O = {2+-1 | -2+-1} in both trees) cannot be obtained from the paper's own definition.

In the e.p.-aware tree 21 end positions are class N (class counts L/R/N/draw = 60/42/21/3 in realchess/results/comp_Wa2c2_Bb7d7_oracleall_pure_epaware_offline.json), so a single t would change them. Add that Lemma 17 lets any such end position be any game in [-2BIG, 2BIG].

verdict.reason: Could not refute it. /Users/aritro/Downloads/Research/Chessendgames/paper/ieee/sections/09_real.tex lines 10-12 say every end position that is not L or R is replaced by "one fixed game t", and call that choice "the draw treatment". That set contains mover-wins (N), mover-loses (P) and drawn positions, so N is not a draw and the name is wrong for it. The oracle the evidence computes treats the classes separately. realchess/oracle_value.py docstring (lines 12-17) and TREATMENTS/pair_game (lines ~604-646): L -> +BIG, R -> -BIG, N -> {+BIG | -BIG}, P -> 0, and only draws take the treatment (draw as Black win, draw as White win, draw as 0, or "free", where every non-L/R terminal is any game in [-2BIG, 2BIG]). realchess/REPORT.md section 6 "Treatments, and why" says the same. The e.p.-aware tree has L/R/N/draw = 60/42/21/3 (realchess/results/comp_Wa2c2_Bb7d7_oracleall_pure_epaware_offline.json, class_counts), so 21 end positions are N. Theorem 18(c) ("draws count as wins for black", O = {2+-1 | -2+-1} in both trees) is the "switch, draw = Black win" treatment (realchess/REPORT.md claim C3). It needs N to be the switch and the 3 draws (White to move draws, Black to move wins) to be -BIG. verdict.better_fix: Replace lines 10-12 of 09_real.tex (from "Replace each end position" to "the draw treatment.") with: "Replace each end position by $+\BIG$ if white wins it in real chess with either side to move, by $-\BIG$ if black does, by $\game{+\BIG}{-\BIG}$ if the side to move wins, and by $0$ if the side to move loses. Optionally, 18(b) can add "and even if every end position that is not $\pm\BIG$ is any game in $[-2\BIG,2\BIG]$", which realchess/REPORT.md section 0 item 3 supports."

rejected.quote: the defender cannot promote anywhere within $h$ moves (the \emph{counter-promotion condition})
rejected.why:
Refuted as an inconsistency. It is a worry about an unproven conjecture, and the proposed fix would create a real contradiction.

1. The printed condition is exactly the one in the evidence. The paper's "cannot promote anywhere within h moves" is (L2) mu_s >= T+1 of Definition 2.6 / Theorem 2.7 in kings/theory/LOOPY.md (lines 664-666). Counting who moves first, it has no off-by-one against LOOPY. kings/REPORT.md lines 50-51 states the certificate in the same words: "the defender cannot promote anywhere in T moves", and "its proof still has a gap". The paper's "Our proof of this has a gap" is the project's own current status. LOOPY's T2.7 row is still "GAP (proof incomplete)".

2. The margin T+2 is only a recommendation. LOOPY line 667 calls (L2+) "the recommended margin before invoking (A_Q)". It is not part of Theorem 2.7 and not a requirement. The only support is a plausibility remark, "queen-against-seventh-rank-pawn endings can be drawn". No file records a chess position that meets mu = T+1 and still fails. LOOPY lines 1236-1237 only conjecture that the real trebuchet failures sit at margin one, and say how to settle it. So "may be false" is true of any conjecture, and the paper already labels this one Conj and says it is unproven. The auditor himself says the label is fine.

3. The T30 row is not endorsed. notes/proof_audit2/REPORT.md puts the verifier first, and it takes precedence. The verifier says the Conj 5 claims were "Not checked, so not endorsed" because the table was truncated. The agent text itself says only "chess version likely needs a margin". delegate/REVIEW.md (round 7, T30 row) records the other T30 fixes and adopts no change to this conjecture.

4. The proposed fix "cannot promote within h+1 moves" would break Proposition 6 (prop:horizon1). That proposition says that for h=1 the counter-promotion condition holds in every chess-legal context without a passed pawn on boards with six or more ranks. Its proof only rules out a pawn one move from promotion, which is mu >= 2 = T+1. LOOPY lines 763-764 say outright that mu_s >= 2 "is enough for (L2), though not always for the margin (L2+)". With the margin, h=1 would require mu >= 3. A context such as W a6 / B b7 (white a6 not passed, two moves from promotion) violates it on 8 ranks. The paper's "counter-promotion condition" term is defined on lines 88-89 and reused in Proposition 6, so changing it there changes the proposition too. The second option, "in the promotion model", does not fit either. The paper never defines a promotion model, and (V3) is defined as "in chess, every move in Z loses".

5. "Gap" does not understate beyond the project's own wording. The chess bridge (A_Q) is a per-position hypothesis that is false in general (LOOPY line 29). The examples are Ke2 Pb5 ka5 and Kd1 Pb3 ka3, where the pawn promotes but the king captures the new queen. The certificate's (L1) already requires a queen the defender cannot capture at once. The paper's one-line "has a gap" is the same level of detail as kings/REPORT.md.

Verdict: no inconsistency between the paper and the evidence. At most this is an optional hedge on a conjecture, with severity below low.
